validity.recommendation: change Status from 'operating' to 'retired' (as a gas pipeline) -- Trailblazer has been formally abandoned by FERC and physically repurposed to transport CO2, not natural gas; this is exactly the batch brief's flagged lead for P0266
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: unambiguous -- the pipeline is real, active infrastructure today (just not carrying gas). DUPLICATE: checked against the full 46-row roster (P0151...P3601) -- no separate 'Trailblazer CO2' or similarly-named row exists, so this is not a redundancy question, only a status/classification one on this same row. CLASSIFICATION/STATUS (the batch brief's central lead): Tallgrass announced in 2022 that it would convert Trailblazer from natural gas to CO2 transport service. S&P Global (2022-06-01, via Wayback) reported Trailblazer Pipeline Company LLC and Rockies Express Pipeline LLC filed for FERC authorization (Docket CP22-468, filed 2022-05-27) to abandon ~392 miles of the Trailblazer gas system in place and repurpose it for CO2, while gas shippers were to be rerouted onto new REX leased capacity/laterals. FERC's own Federal Register notice (2023-04-06) confirms an Environmental Assessment was issued for 'Trailblazer Pipeline Company LLC, Rockies Express Pipeline LLC' covering this conversion. A second Federal Register notice (2024-10-09) confirms FERC's October 23, 2023 Order 'Issuing Certificate and Granting Abandonment' authorized the project (the 'Trailblazer Conversion Project' in Weld County, CO and Kimball County, NE), that construction began January 4, 2024, and that Trailblazer/REX requested (and were later granted, per the docket) an extension to complete the Hereford Ranch and Redtail Compressor Stations by December 23, 2024. Oil & Gas Journal (2024-05-06, via Wayback since the live OGJ URL serves randomized unrelated article content to non-browser fetches) reported Trailblazer/REX holding a CO2 transport open season under the FERC-approved conversion, confirming the project moved from authorization into commercialization. ADM's own investor-facing overview PDF states the timeline plainly: '2022 Announce Project ... 2024 Begin CO2 Service' and that the project 'converts the nearly 400-mile Trailblazer pipeline from natural gas service to carbon dioxide (CO2)... to permanently store more than 10 million metric tons of CO2 annually.' Nebraska Examiner (2025-09-24 and 2025-10-10) both independently confirm commercial CO2 shipments began October 3, 2025, moving CO2 from 11 Nebraska/Colorado/Wyoming ethanol plants ~392 miles to Wyoming for sequestration, explicitly stating 'the Trailblazer pipeline formerly carried natural gas' and 'much of the pipeline was already built as the natural gas line.' Pipeline & Gas Journal (2025-09, verified separately) restates the same 392-mile CO2-transport-begins story. Six independent origins (FERC/Federal Register x2, S&P Global, OGJ, ADM, Nebraska Examiner/PGJ) converge: Trailblazer is no longer in gas service. Per docs/reference/controlled_vocab.md, 'retired' is the correct Status value for a formally abandoned/decommissioned gas asset -- there is no 'converted' or repurposed-commodity value in the Status vocab, and this GGIT (gas) tracker is not the place to add a new CO2 row for the same pipe; that is a separate tracking-scope question for Baird, not resolved here. GEM's LastUpdated=2023-08-30 predates the October 2023 abandonment order and the 2024-2025 physical conversion/start of CO2 service, which is why the sheet is now stale rather than simply wrong-when-entered. NOTE for the batch brief's cross-reference: P0208 (TIGT/Pony Express Abandonment, Docket CP12-495, 2012-2014) is a DIFFERENT, EARLIER Tallgrass gas-to-crude conversion of a different pipeline (TIGT, not Trailblazer) -- confirmed by direct comparison of the two FERC dockets and Tallgrass's own 2016 10-K; the two conversions should not be conflated, and this row's finding stands independently of that one.

validity.recommendation: change StartState/Province from 'Wyoming' to 'Colorado' -- three independent sources place Trailblazer's origin in Colorado, not Wyoming
validity.researcher_notes: GEM currently carries StartLocation='Cheyenne', StartState/Province='Wyoming'. Three independent origins instead describe a Colorado origin: (1) OSTI/DOE trade-journal abstract (1982): 'the Trailblazer Pipeline Co. 436-mile section from Rockport, Colo. to Beatrice [Neb.]'; (2) Tallgrass's own historical company-overview page (via a 2019-07-27 Wayback snapshot, since the live pipeline.tallgrassenergylp.com is now behind an Incapsula bot-wall for both live and later-dated Wayback crawls): 'Trailblazer Pipeline Company LLC (Trailblazer) is a 436-mile pipeline extending from northeast Colorado to Gage County in Nebraska'; (3) Wikipedia's (en.wikipedia.org, independent of GEM/gem.wiki) 'Trailblazer Pipeline' stub, categorized under 'Natural gas pipelines in Colorado' and 'Natural gas pipelines in Nebraska' (NOT Wyoming), stating plainly it 'brings natural gas from Colorado into Nebraska.' The one source in tension with this is Tallgrass's own 2015 SEC S-1 registration statement, which hedges: 'The Trailblazer Pipeline is a FERC-regulated natural gas pipeline system with approximately 436-miles of transportation pipelines that begins along the border of Wyoming and Colorado and extends to Beatrice, Nebraska' -- consistent with an origin very close to the state line (Cheyenne, WY sits only a few miles north of the CO border; Rockport, CO sits just south of it) but not itself naming Wyoming as the state of origin. Weighing three independent, more specific sources (a contemporaneous trade journal, Tallgrass's own historical company page, and Wikipedia) against one hedged company-filing sentence, Colorado is the better-supported StartState/Province. Not proposing a specific StartLocation replacement (e.g. 'Rockport') given the S-1's own border-region framing and no fully independent second source for that particular place name -- leaving StartLocation as a lower-confidence open question rather than overreaching. EndLocation='Beatrice'/EndState/Province='Nebraska' are NOT contested -- all three of the above sources, plus the S-1, agree on the Nebraska/Beatrice-area terminus (the 2019 Tallgrass page's 'Gage County' is the same place -- Beatrice is the Gage County seat).

validity.recommendation: change StartYear1 from 1981 to 1982 -- the OSTI trade-journal source gives an explicit October 1982 completion date for the whole Trailblazer system, consistent with a 1981-1982 construction span rather than a 1981 in-service date
validity.researcher_notes: A federal-court opinion (Colo. Interstate Gas v. Natural Gas Pipeline Co., 661 F. Supp. 1448, D. Wyo. 1987, via Justia) states: 'In 1981-1982 a new pipeline, the Trailblazer System, was constructed to transport natural gas out of the Overthrust region of Wyoming.' The OSTI/DOE trade-journal abstract is more specific and gives a completion date: '...for an October 1982 completion date, the 36-in. Trailblazer pipeline system consists of three major segments...' Read together, construction began in 1981 (supporting a new ConstructionYear fill of 1981, below) and the system entered service/was completed in October 1982 -- not 1981 as GEM's StartYear1 currently states. Both sources describe the whole three-segment Trailblazer System (Overthrust + Wyoming Interstate/WIC + Trailblazer proper) as a single coordinated 1981-82 construction/completion event, so the October 1982 date applies to this Trailblazer segment as well. Tier kept at medium/high rather than higher because neither source gives a month-specific in-service date for the Trailblazer segment ALONE as distinct from the three-segment system, though OSTI's 'October 1982 completion date' is stated for the system as a whole in the same sentence that names the Trailblazer segment specifically.

validity.recommendation: clear FuelSource -- 'Colorado' is a state name, not an upstream field/plant/facility, and violates the documented GEM schema convention for this column
validity.researcher_notes: Per docs/reference/gem_schema.md's explicit documented gotcha, FuelSource (gas sheet) must name the upstream gas source feeding the line -- a specific field, plant, or facility (e.g. 'Abqaiq', 'Berri Gas Plant') -- and must NEVER be a state name or the commodity type. GEM's current value 'Colorado' is a state, not a named field/facility, so it is a schema-convention violation independent of the classification finding above. I could not confidently attribute a single named upstream field: Trailblazer historically received Rocky Mountain/Overthrust-belt gas (per the OSTI/Justia sources on the original three-segment Trailblazer System) via multiple interconnects rather than one dedicated field, and ADM's project-overview map depicts 'Cheyenne Hub' (a well-known multi-source trading/interconnect hub in the DJ Basin straddling the CO/WY line) near the pipeline's origin, but no source I found states outright that Cheyenne Hub (or any other single named point) IS Trailblazer's FuelSource in the GEM sense. Recommending the cell be cleared (left blank) rather than replaced with an unverified guess, per the schema doc's own instruction ('if you can't attribute one, leave it blank and note why -- do not default it'). This is also now moot with respect to the CO2 conversion: whichever way the classification question above is resolved, FuelSource as currently entered is a defect either way.

validity.recommendation: flag Capacity=878 MMcf/d as unconfirmed -- Tallgrass's own 2015 SEC S-1 states a different figure (902 MMcf/d) for the same pipeline
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's current Capacity (878.00 MMcf/d) could not be confirmed by any source I found. Tallgrass Energy Partners LP's SEC S-1 (filed 2015-02-24, CIK 0001633651) instead states: 'The Trailblazer Pipeline is a FERC-regulated natural gas pipeline system with approximately 436-miles of transportation pipelines that begins along the border of Wyoming and Colorado and extends to Beatrice, Nebraska with a total system design capacity of approximately 902 MMcf/d' (as of Dec 31, 2014). This is the pipeline's own regulated-entity's SEC disclosure, not a secondary aggregator, but it is a single origin, and I could not find a second independent source stating either 878 or 902 with confidence (a widely-mirrored 'design capacity as of 2016' figure of 878 MMcf/d traces to grokipedia.com, an AI-generated wiki that is not a citable/verifiable primary or secondary source, so I am not treating it as corroboration for GEM's existing value). Not proposing a firm replacement given the single-source status -- flagging the conflict so whoever next touches Capacity knows 878 is unconfirmed and 902 (2014-vintage, per the S-1) is the best-sourced alternative found so far.
